words.meaning: to restore goodwill or reduce hostility through a considerate action or approach
words.example: The director met with the frustrated vendors to conciliate them before renegotiating the contract.
The newsroom took on a febrile atmosphere as election results began arriving.

words.meaning: to break out or become active again after a period of improvement
words.example: The dispute may recrudesce if both departments stop sharing their budget data.

words.meaning: behaving as though you are superior to other people
words.example: His supercilious tone alienated colleagues who had tried to help him.

words.meaning: extremely loud and powerful in sound, especially describing a voice
words.example: Her stentorian announcement carried across the crowded terminal without a microphone.

phrases.meaning: to stop working properly, usually because of a mechanical or electronic problem
phrases.example: Our office printer always seems to go on the fritz right before a major deadline.

phrases.meaning: to fail badly or give a disappointing performance
phrases.example: The comedian laid an egg at the first show but won over the late-night crowd.

phrases.meaning: to deliberately avoid taking action when action is needed
phrases.example: We cannot sit on our hands while support requests continue to pile up.

phrases.meaning: to be hit hard or badly shaken by a physical or figurative blow
phrases.example: The company got its bell rung when its largest customer switched suppliers.

phrases.meaning: in a very large quantity or to an excessive degree
phrases.example: That new phone has advanced features out the wazoo, but most buyers use only a few.
